title: Conflicts
blurb: Both conflict kinds, resolved. A Workspace on feature changes the page heading while an fs edit changes the same line on the Branch, so its commit is refused Conflict and leaves markers; the agent keeps its own line, clears the markers and commits. Then header edits that line too, so merging feature and header is refused until header agrees, and the merge is published.
prompt: Change the page heading on feature, and resolve whatever conflicts that causes with the edits already on the Branch and on header. Keep our line, then merge feature and header and publish the result.

bash.description: sb1: open a Workspace on feature and change the heading
bash.command:
layerfs sandbox create | tee sandbox.json
layerfs workspace mount "$(jq -r .sandbox sandbox.json)" feature | tee mount.json
layerfs workspace exec "$(jq -r .ws mount.json)" "sed -i 's/Hello world/Hello from the Workspace/' app/page.tsx" --stream

root.note: The Workspace and its Sandbox stay up with the uncommitted edit: the conflict is shown across the next steps.

bash.description: fs on feature: edit app/page.tsx "Hello world" "Hello from fs"
bash.command: layerfs fs edit feature /app/page.tsx --old 'Hello world' --new 'Hello from fs' -m "edit /app/page.tsx"
layerfs workspace commit {{ws}} -m "sb1: change the heading"

bash.description: sb1: keep the Workspace's heading, clear the markers and commit
bash.command:
layerfs workspace exec {{ws}} "sed -i '/Hello from fs\|^<<<<<<<\|^=======\|^>>>>>>>/d' app/page.tsx" --stream
layerfs workspace commit {{ws}} -m "sb1: keep the Workspace's heading"

bash.description: sb1: unmount and close the Sandbox
bash.command:
layerfs workspace unmount {{ws}}
layerfs sandbox close {{sandbox}}

bash.description: fs on header: edit app/page.tsx "Hello world" "Hello from header"
bash.command: layerfs fs edit header /app/page.tsx --old 'Hello world' --new 'Hello from header' -m "edit /app/page.tsx"

bash.description: Merge feature and header as release
bash.command: layerfs branch merge feature header release

bash.description: fs on header: edit app/page.tsx "Hello from header" "Hello from the Workspace"
bash.command: layerfs fs edit header /app/page.tsx --old 'Hello from header' --new 'Hello from the Workspace' -m "edit /app/page.tsx"

bash.description: Merge feature and header as release
bash.command: layerfs branch merge feature header release

root.reply: Both conflicts are resolved and release is on main.
